review.why: Writes reliable n8n expressions: reference data by node name, avoid pointless Set nodes, use Luxon for dates, and format long expressions with comments.
review.summary: Its core rule is to reference data with the node name instead of the current item, with a no-op anchor where branches converge. It names the Set-node antipattern and when a Set earns its place, then shows single-field transforms and array method chains, with advice to indent and comment multi-step expressions. Date handling uses Luxon rather than a date node.
strengths: Explains the silent breakage of current-item references after refactors
Quick test for whether a Set node is needed
Examples of commented multi-line expressions for non-coders
cautions: Only the first part was read here; later sections are not covered
